findings.title: Object/array property (key) names are never sanitized, only their values
findings.explanation: The whole purpose of this package, as stated in package.json/README, is to sanitize req.body/req.query/req.params/req.headers so attacker-supplied HTML/JS cannot reach the application unescaped. In the object branch of sanitize(), only the value `item = data[key]` is run through sanitizeHtml(); the property name `key` itself is taken verbatim from Object.keys(data) and reused unchanged when building the result (`data[key] = ...`). For req.body (JSON) and req.query (URL-encoded query string) the attacker fully controls the key names, e.g. a JSON body of {"":1} or a query string of ?=1 produces an object whose malicious key survives the middleware untouched. Any application code that reflects object/array keys into an HTML response (debug/admin views that dump Object.keys(req.query) or req.body, form-field-name echoing, log/report viewers, etc.) remains exploitable to XSS even after this 'xss sanitizer' middleware has run, giving developers a false sense of safety.
